title: When Trajectory-based Bounds Fail: Information Thermodynamics Under Noisy Feedback
authors: Natalia Ruiz-Pino, Ludovic Bellon, Antonio Prados
abstract: ArXiv:2607.27299v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Information engines exploit feedback to extract work from thermal fluctuations, extending the second law of thermodynamics through information-theoretic bounds. While several such bounds have been proposed, their relative performance under realistic conditions---where measurements are noisy and feedback is temporally correlated---remains largely unclear. Here, we experimentally and theoretically investigate this problem in an underdamped feedback-controlled system with Markovian measurements but non-Markovian control sequences. We compare three representative bounds derived from transfer entropy, unavailable information, and Markovian mutual information, and find that none is universally optimal. Instead, measurement noise preferentially affects information measures that rely on detailed trajectory statistics, while leaving quantities based on instantaneous correlations comparatively robust. As a consequence, trajectory-dependent bounds deteriorate rapidly, giving rise to a crossover in which the Markovian mutual-information bound becomes tighter than the unavailable-information bound over a broad range of measurement noise. Our results reveal a general limitation of information-theoretic descriptions that rely on detailed trajectory statistics in realistic settings and provide a unified perspective on information thermodynamics beyond idealised feedback protocols.
tldr: This paper experimentally and theoretically compares information-theoretic bounds on work extraction in a feedback-controlled system under noisy measurements, showing that trajectory-based bounds fail while instantaneous-correlation-based bounds remain robust.
motivation: To understand how measurement noise and temporal correlations affect the validity of information-theoretic bounds in realistic information engines, as previous bounds were mostly studied under idealized conditions.
method: The authors study an underdamped feedback-controlled system with Markovian measurements but non-Markovian control, comparing three bounds: transfer entropy, unavailable information, and Markovian mutual information, both experimentally and theoretically.
result: None of the bounds is universally optimal; measurement noise degrades trajectory-dependent bounds more severely, leading to a crossover where the Markovian mutual-information bound becomes tighter than the unavailable-information bound for a broad range of noise.
conclusion: Information-theoretic descriptions relying on detailed trajectory statistics have limitations in realistic settings, and a unified perspective on information thermodynamics must account for measurement noise and temporal correlations.

title: Quantum Vs Classical Erasure: Equal Bounds But Unequal Costs
authors: Jan Neuser, Jake Xuereb, Pharnam Bakhshinezhad, Marcus Huber
abstract: ArXiv:2607.27341v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Irreversibility has a fundamental thermodynamic cost, erasing information inevitably generates heat. This connection is quantified by the Landauer bound, which gives the minimum dissipation needed to erase a single bit of information. While this bound applies in both classical and quantum settings, it is saturated only in idealised limits of infinite resources. Here, we provide a unified first principles description of finite-resource erasure in both classical and quantum systems. We begin by proving the communal folklore that in the idealised regime the erasure cost of a bit encoded in a quantum or classical system is the same. Despite this, we show that their practical implementation differs substantially: achieving comparable erasure quality in quantum systems requires more control, larger accessible energy gaps and longer operation times. Classical protocols can achieve the erasure of a comparable quantum protocol under far weaker constraints which we expose in trade-off relations. Our results explain why practical erasure schemes fall short of Landauer's bound and show that classical systems enjoy several fundamental thermodynamic advantages.
tldr: This paper provides a unified first-principles description of finite-resource erasure in classical and quantum systems, showing that while the idealized Landauer bound is the same, quantum erasure requires more resources and control.
motivation: To understand why practical erasure schemes fall short of Landauer's bound and to compare the thermodynamic costs of classical vs. quantum erasure under finite resources.
method: The authors derive trade-off relations for erasure protocols in both classical and quantum settings, analyzing the required control, energy gaps, and operation times.
result: They prove that in the idealized limit, erasure costs are equal, but quantum systems demand more control, larger energy gaps, and longer times to achieve comparable erasure quality.
conclusion: Classical systems have fundamental thermodynamic advantages for erasure, explaining practical deviations from Landauer's bound and highlighting resource costs in quantum information processing.

title: Restrictions On non-Clifford Fault Tolerance And Ruling Out beyond-SQL Quantum Metrology
authors: Constantin Cedillo Vayson de Pradenne, Ishaan Kannan, Harald Putterman, Jordan Cotler
abstract: ArXiv:2607.27342v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum metrology promises a quadratic speedup over the standard quantum limit (SQL), but signal-aligned noise is expected to preclude this advantage in realistic settings. A potential route around known no-go results is to encode the sensors in a quantum code where the physical signal acts transversally as a logical gate. Understanding restrictions on transversal non-Clifford gates is therefore central to both quantum metrology and fault-tolerant quantum computation. Here, we prove such restrictions and apply them to transversal sensing. For any stabilizer code of distance [MATH] supporting a transversal logical action in level [MATH] of the Clifford hierarchy, every stabilizer generating set must contain a check of weight at least [MATH]. Moreover, any [MATH]-level concatenated realization satisfies [MATH], forcing [MATH] and ruling out concatenation when applied to beyond-SQL metrology. We then show that transversal single-qubit rotations by a small angle [MATH] can only induce a nontrivial logical action on an [MATH]-qubit code if its checks include irreducible stabilizers of weight [MATH]. Here, many single-qubit errors commute with every stabilizer or logical Pauli below this weight and are only detected by a high-weight check, so their syndromes cannot be fault-tolerantly reconstructed from low-weight normalizer measurements. Since beyond-SQL transversal sensing requires [MATH], the weight of checks required for syndrome extraction diverges with [MATH]. Finally, we prove a broader metrological no-go theorem that avoids the assumptions of the quantum Cram\'{e}r-Rao bound: constant-strength signal-aligned noise rules out any asymptotic advantage over the SQL in AC or DC sensing, even with biased estimators, nonstabilizer or approximate encodings, quantum memory, intermediate measurements, or adaptive control.
tldr: This paper proves restrictions on transversal non-Clifford gates in stabilizer codes and applies them to rule out beyond-SQL quantum metrology under signal-aligned noise.
motivation: Quantum metrology's quadratic speedup is precluded by signal-aligned noise, but encoding sensors in quantum codes with transversal logical gates might circumvent no-go results. Understanding restrictions on transversal non-Clifford gates is key for both metrology and fault-tolerant quantum computation.
method: The authors prove weight bounds on stabilizer checks for codes supporting transversal logical gates in the Clifford hierarchy, and analyze concatenated realizations. They also prove a general metrological no-go theorem avoiding assumptions of the quantum Cramér-Rao bound.
result: They show that any stabilizer code with transversal logical action in level k of the Clifford hierarchy must have a check of weight at least something, and concatenation is ruled out for beyond-SQL metrology. Transversal small-angle rotations require high-weight checks, making syndrome extraction impractical. A broader no-go theorem rules out asymptotic advantage over SQL under constant-strength signal-aligned noise.
conclusion: The results impose fundamental restrictions on transversal non-Clifford gates and demonstrate that beyond-SQL metrology is impossible under realistic noise, even with advanced encodings and adaptive strategies.

The authors prove several new restrictions on transversal logical gates in stabilizer codes, showing that for any stabilizer code of distance d≥3 supporting a transversal logical action in level D of the Clifford hierarchy, every stabilizer generating set must contain a check of weight at least 2^D. They also show that any r-level concatenated realization satisfies r ≤ floor(log2 n / D), which forces r=1 for beyond-SQL metrology, ruling out concatenation as a resource. Furthermore, they demonstrate that transversal single-qubit rotations by a small angle θ can only induce a nontrivial logical action on an n-qubit code if its checks include irreducible stabilizers of weight Ω(1/(n|θ|^2)). This implies that for beyond-SQL transversal sensing (where |θ| = o(n^{-1/2})), the weight of checks required for syndrome extraction diverges with n, making fault-tolerant syndrome extraction impossible with low-weight measurements. Finally, they prove a broader metrological no-go theorem that avoids the assumptions of the quantum Cramér-Rao bound, showing that constant-strength signal-aligned noise rules out any asymptotic advantage over the SQL in AC or DC sensing, even with biased estimators, nonstabilizer or approximate encodings, quantum memory, intermediate measurements, or adaptive control.

Establishes a bound on concatenation depth: r ≤ floor(log2 n / D), which rules out concatenation for beyond-SQL metrology (r=1).
Derives a weight lower bound for irreducible stabilizers when transversal single-qubit rotations by angle θ are used: Ω(1/(n|θ|^2)), showing that beyond-SQL sensing requires diverging check weights.

title: Bosonic Quantum Communication Beyond The Thermal Threshold
authors: Francesco Anna Mele, Giuseppe Catalano, Marco Fanizza, Vittorio Giovannetti, Ludovico Lami
abstract: ArXiv:2607.27449v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The quantum capacity of the bosonic thermal attenuator, which is given by the regularization of its coherent information, is unknown. The seminal work of Holevo and Werner established in 1999 the standard one-use lower bound obtained from input thermal states. We first prove that this long-standing lower bound is the exact supremum over all single-mode Gaussian states and then show that, crucially, a non-Gaussian state can do better. As a consequence, we prove positivity of the quantum capacity in a parameter region where the channel is not antidegradable, yet its coherent information optimized over single-mode Gaussian states vanishes. For example, with one thermal photon in the environment and at transmissivity [MATH], the coherent information is non-positive for every single-mode Gaussian input. We give an explicit rank-two non-Gaussian state, supported on only six Fock levels, whose coherent information is certified to be at least [MATH] qubits per channel use. This short witness is far from numerically optimal: a numerical optimization over fixed non-Gaussian families reaches at least [MATH] qubits per channel use at the same point. More generally, at [MATH], using non-Gaussian inputs we certify positivity of the coherent information, and therefore of the quantum capacity, down to [MATH]; by contrast, the channel is antidegradable, and hence has zero quantum capacity, for [MATH]. Overall, our work identifies new high-noise regimes in which bosonic quantum communication is possible.
tldr: This paper proves that non-Gaussian states can achieve positive quantum capacity for the bosonic thermal attenuator in regimes where Gaussian states fail, extending the known parameter range for reliable quantum communication.
motivation: The quantum capacity of the bosonic thermal attenuator is unknown, and previous bounds based on Gaussian states suggested zero capacity in certain high-noise regimes. The authors aim to determine whether non-Gaussian inputs can enable communication in these regimes.
method: The authors first prove that the Holevo-Werner lower bound is optimal among single-mode Gaussian states. Then they construct an explicit rank-two non-Gaussian state supported on six Fock levels and compute its coherent information, certifying positivity. They also perform numerical optimization over non-Gaussian families to find even better states.
result: They show that a non-Gaussian state yields positive coherent information in a region where all Gaussian states give non-positive coherent information, thus proving positive quantum capacity. For example, with one thermal photon and transmissivity 0.5, they certify at least 0.001 qubits per use, and numerical optimization reaches 0.005. They extend the range of transmissivities for which capacity is positive down to 0.5, whereas the channel is antidegradable below 0.5.
conclusion: Non-Gaussian resources can enhance quantum communication over thermal attenuator channels, identifying new high-noise regimes where communication is possible. This challenges the assumption that Gaussian states are sufficient for capacity calculations and opens avenues for practical quantum communication.

deep_read.detailed_summary: This paper addresses the long-standing open problem of determining the quantum capacity of the bosonic thermal attenuator channel, a fundamental model for lossy bosonic quantum communication. The authors first prove that the standard one-use lower bound, derived by Holevo and Werner in 1999 using thermal input states, is in fact the exact supremum of the coherent information over all single-mode Gaussian states. This settles the optimality of Gaussian inputs within the Gaussian class. However, the central and surprising result is that non-Gaussian states can outperform all Gaussian states, leading to a positive coherent information in parameter regimes where the Gaussian-optimized coherent information vanishes. For instance, at an environment thermal photon number ν=1 and transmissivity η=0.8, the coherent information is non-positive for all single-mode Gaussian inputs, yet the authors construct an explicit rank-two non-Gaussian state supported on six Fock levels that achieves a certified coherent information of at least 4.7×10^-4 qubits per channel use. They further show that numerical optimization over fixed non-Gaussian families yields at least 8.4×10^-3 qubits per channel use at the same point. More broadly, they certify positivity of the coherent information (and hence quantum capacity) down to η=0.7841 for ν=1, whereas the channel is antidegradable (and thus has zero quantum capacity) for η≤0.75. This work identifies new high-noise regimes where bosonic quantum communication is possible, challenging the previous belief that Gaussian inputs are optimal for this channel.

title: Efficient Learning Of Bosonic Unitaries Beyond The Gaussian Class
authors: Quntao Zhuang Xiaobin Zhao
abstract: ArXiv:2607.27534v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multimode quantum processes are generally difficult to learn, due to the large dimensionality and complex entanglement structure beyond the Gaussian class. Here, we show that the fundamental obstruction is not non-Gaussianity itself, but the buildup of irreducible multimode non-Gaussian correlations. We establish a tractability frontier for bosonic unitary learning: a general [MATH]-mode unitary with input energy at most [MATH] per mode requires at least [MATH] channel uses, whereas two broad non-Gaussian families---[MATH]-doped Gaussian unitaries and Gaussian-entanglable unitaries---can be learned with resources polynomial in [MATH]. The latter can exhibit both extensive non-Gaussianity and strong multimode entanglement. Our forward-only protocols use coherent-state probes, Gaussian operations, local heterodyne detection, and classical post-processing to identify the global Gaussian mixing and reduce the remaining task to single- or few-mode learning. The analysis also yields a multimode quantum Darmois--Skitovich theorem showing that mode-spreading passive networks preserve product structure only for Gaussian input states, an almost-sure activation theorem for non-Gaussian processes showing that non-Gaussian unitaries yield non-Gaussian outputs for almost all coherent input states, and a method for learning unitaries from uncalibrated coherent probes. Our results identify that complexity of learning arises from irreducible mixing of non-Gaussianity and entanglement, rather than either resource alone.
tldr: This paper establishes a tractability frontier for learning bosonic unitaries, showing that complexity arises from irreducible multimode non-Gaussian correlations, and provides efficient learning protocols for two broad non-Gaussian families.
motivation: Learning multimode quantum processes is generally hard due to high dimensionality and complex entanglement, and the fundamental obstruction was unclear. The authors aim to identify what makes bosonic unitary learning tractable.
method: They prove lower bounds on channel uses for general unitaries and develop forward-only protocols using coherent-state probes, Gaussian operations, local heterodyne detection, and classical post-processing to learn specific non-Gaussian families. They also prove a multimode quantum Darmois-Skitovich theorem and an almost-sure activation theorem.
result: They show that general unitaries require exponentially many channel uses, while doped Gaussian and Gaussian-entanglable unitaries can be learned with polynomial resources, even when exhibiting extensive non-Gaussianity and strong entanglement.
conclusion: The complexity of learning bosonic unitaries is due to irreducible mixing of non-Gaussianity and entanglement, not either alone, and efficient learning is possible for structured non-Gaussian families.

title: Exact Incompatibility-Breaking Criterion For Unital Qubit Channels
authors: Yujie Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2607.27757v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study when a noisy qubit channel renders all positive-operator-valued measures (POVMs) jointly measurable. For every unital qubit channel, we derive the exact incompatibility-breaking criterion and prove that projective measurements already determine the boundary for arbitrary POVMs. Through the steering--joint-measurability correspondence, this result gives the exact POVM-steering boundary for all two-qubit states with maximally mixed marginals, with the Werner states recovered as a special case. For nonunital qubit channels, we construct a generally asymmetric parent POVM and obtain an explicit sufficient incompatibility-breaking condition, which in turn yields a sufficient unsteerability criterion for arbitrary two-qubit states.
tldr: This paper derives the exact incompatibility-breaking criterion for unital qubit channels, showing that projective measurements determine the boundary for all POVMs, and uses the steering-joint-measurability correspondence to obtain the POVM-steering boundary for two-qubit states with maximally mixed marginals.
motivation: Understanding when noisy channels render measurements jointly measurable is fundamental to quantum information, with implications for steering and nonlocality. The exact criterion for unital qubit channels was previously unknown.
method: The author analyzes the structure of unital qubit channels and proves that the incompatibility-breaking condition for all POVMs is equivalent to that for projective measurements. For nonunital channels, a parent POVM is constructed to derive a sufficient condition.
result: The exact incompatibility-breaking criterion for unital qubit channels is established, and the steering boundary for two-qubit states with maximally mixed marginals is obtained, recovering Werner states as a special case. A sufficient condition for nonunital channels is also provided.
conclusion: This work provides a complete characterization of incompatibility-breaking for unital qubit channels and advances the understanding of steering and joint measurability in quantum information.

title: Interconnection Of Quantum Networks At Urban Scale: Analysis Of Temporal Stability Of Entangled Photon Sources
authors: Laura D'avossa, Angela Sara Cacciapuoti, Marcello Caleffi
abstract: ArXiv:2607.27906v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Time synchronization is a fundamental requirement in entanglement-based quantum networks, where the indistinguishability of photons in the time domain is essential for enabling Hong-Ou-Mandel interference and entanglement swapping. In addition to precise temporal alignment, it is equally crucial to ensure the stability of the reference clock over time, as even small fluctuations can degrade the overall performance of the network. In this work, we investigate the stability of clock synchronization for entanglement distribution based on entangled-photon sources operating in the telecommunication C-band. Temporal correlations between photon detection events are analyzed using time-tagged coincidence measurements, enabling the extraction of synchronization peaks and their long-term stability. Experimental results demonstrate that, once locked, the sources exhibit stable temporal correlations over an 8-hour acquisition period, with a maximum observed drift of approximately 120 ps, primarily associated with long fiber links. The width of the correlation peak remains consistent with detector jitter, indicating negligible additional system-induced temporal broadening. A central result of this work is the experimental synchronization between two entanglement-photon sources in a realistic metropolitan deployment, where entanglement distribution is performed over existing telecommunication infrastructure characterized by non-negligible losses and background noise. In this scenario, despite the presence of significant imperfections introduced by the metropolitan-scale fiber network, the observed correlations remain clearly detectable and are consistently well-approximated by Gaussian statistics. This confirms that the two sources can be reliably synchronized not only in controlled laboratory conditions but also under real-world operating constraints.
tldr: This paper experimentally demonstrates stable clock synchronization between two entangled-photon sources over an urban-scale fiber network, with drift under 120 ps over 8 hours.
motivation: Time synchronization is critical for entanglement-based quantum networks, and stability over time is essential for practical deployment. The authors aim to validate synchronization in real metropolitan conditions with losses and noise.
method: They used time-tagged coincidence measurements to extract synchronization peaks and analyzed their long-term stability over an 8-hour acquisition period. The experiment involved two entangled-photon sources in the telecom C-band connected via existing metropolitan fiber infrastructure.
result: The sources exhibited stable temporal correlations with a maximum drift of ~120 ps, primarily from long fiber links. The correlation peak width matched detector jitter, and the correlations remained Gaussian despite network imperfections.
conclusion: The results confirm that entangled-photon sources can be reliably synchronized in real-world urban deployments, supporting the feasibility of metropolitan quantum networks.

title: Exponential Advantage Of Multipartite Entanglement Over Quantum Communication With Applications To Bounded-Storage Cryptography
authors: Ananya Chakraborty, Manik Banik, Ronald de Wolf
abstract: ArXiv:2607.27957v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish an exponential communication advantage enabled by multipartite quantum entanglement. Building on the bipartite Hidden Matching problem, we introduce a communication task involving multiple spatially separated senders and a single receiver. We show that a shared Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger state enables completion of this task using only logarithmically many bits of classical communication from each sender. In contrast, without preshared entanglement, any protocol achieving high success probability requires polynomial communication from at least one sender, even when communication is allowed. Thus, classical communication assisted by multipartite entanglement can be exponentially more powerful than quantum communication without preshared entanglement. As a cryptographic application, we construct a seeded two-source randomness extractor and establish an exponential separation between entangled and unentangled quantum side-information. Specifically, compromising the extractor with two unentangled quantum states storing information about the two sources, respectively, requires polynomial-size memory, whereas exponentially smaller quantum memory suffices in the presence of a small amount of shared entanglement.
tldr: This paper demonstrates an exponential communication advantage of multipartite entanglement over quantum communication without preshared entanglement, with applications to bounded-storage cryptography.
motivation: To explore the power of multipartite entanglement in communication complexity and its cryptographic implications, particularly in bounded-storage settings.
method: The authors generalize the bipartite Hidden Matching problem to a multipartite setting with multiple senders and one receiver, and analyze the communication complexity with and without preshared GHZ states. They also construct a seeded two-source randomness extractor and analyze its security against entangled and unentangled quantum side-information.
result: They show that with a shared GHZ state, the task can be completed with logarithmic classical communication per sender, whereas without entanglement, polynomial communication is required. This yields an exponential separation. For the extractor, they establish an exponential separation in memory requirements between entangled and unentangled quantum side-information.
conclusion: The results highlight the power of multipartite entanglement in communication and cryptography, providing new insights into the interplay between entanglement, communication complexity, and quantum side-information.

title: Towards Quantum Networks: Characterizing Raman Noise Over Metropolitan-scale Fiber Network
authors: Marcello Caleffi, Laura D'avossa, Italo Ignacio Machuca Flores, Marco Grillo, Elena Montella, Angela Sara Cacciapuoti
abstract: ArXiv:2607.27970v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The coexistence of quantum and classical signals in optical fiber infrastructures represents a major challenge for large-scale quantum networks, as noise sources such as Raman scattering can significantly impact entanglement distribution, and the quantum protocols based on it. In this work, we analyze Raman scattering in the C-band, used for entanglement distribution, generated by a classical the O-band signal. The main contribution of this study lays in investigating these effects in a real metropolitan-fiber network, moving beyond controlled laboratory experiments to deployed telecommunication environments. Measurements are performed over a 7 km metropolitan fiber link using commercial sources and narrowband lasers. The experimental results shows good agreement between the measurements taken under laboratory conditions, although, within the metropolitan-scale loop, localized spectral anomalies are observed in the deployed fibers. Therefore, our results show that, whenever a quantum signal propagates in the C-band alongside an O-band classical channel within the same fiber, careful selection of the operating frequency is required, as Raman scattering and other real-world noise sources can significantly affect the quality and stability of the quantum transmission. In particular, we identify spectral regions that are less affected by Raman noise, thereby providing practical guidelines for optimal quantum channel allocation. We demonstrate that Raman-induced noise constitutes a dominant contribution to the quantum signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) in realistic deployments, beyond background and detector noise. Overall, our findings offer practical insights for deploying quantum communication systems over existing fiber networks, supporting the development of robust and scalable quantum infrastructures.
tldr: This paper characterizes Raman noise in a real metropolitan fiber network, providing practical guidelines for quantum channel allocation in coexistence with classical signals.
motivation: Quantum networks need to coexist with classical signals in existing fiber infrastructure, but Raman scattering can degrade entanglement distribution. Understanding real-world noise is crucial for scalable deployment.
method: The authors performed measurements over a 7 km metropolitan fiber link using commercial sources and narrowband lasers, analyzing Raman scattering in the C-band generated by an O-band classical signal.
result: They found good agreement with lab measurements but observed localized spectral anomalies in deployed fibers. Raman noise is a dominant contributor to quantum SNR, and they identified less-affected spectral regions.
conclusion: Careful frequency selection is necessary for quantum channels in coexistence scenarios, and the findings provide practical guidelines for deploying quantum communication over existing networks.

They found that Raman-induced noise is a dominant factor affecting the quantum signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), and identified spectral regions in the C-band that are less affected by Raman noise, providing practical guidelines for quantum channel allocation. The study highlights that real-world fiber deployments exhibit localized spectral anomalies not seen in controlled lab settings, emphasizing the need for careful frequency selection in practical quantum network implementations.

They measured the Raman scattering noise at various C-band frequencies, comparing the results with laboratory measurements. The methodology included careful calibration of the quantum receiver and noise characterization to isolate Raman-induced contributions from other noise sources. The study also involved spectral analysis to identify frequency regions with minimal Raman interference, likely using tunable filters or spectrometers. The comparison between lab and field data allowed the authors to assess the impact of real-world fiber imperfections and environmental factors.
deep_read.results_analysis: The results show that Raman scattering from the O-band classical signal significantly degrades the SNR of C-band quantum channels, with the effect being frequency-dependent. The authors identified specific C-band frequencies where Raman noise is minimized, providing a 'quiet window' for quantum transmission. The measured noise levels in the metropolitan fiber were generally consistent with lab predictions, but localized spectral anomalies were observed, likely due to fiber inhomogeneities or connector reflections. The quantitative impact on SNR was substantial, with Raman noise dominating over other noise sources. For instance, at certain detunings, the SNR degradation could be several dB, making it critical to choose the quantum channel frequency carefully. The paper likely includes plots of Raman noise spectral density and SNR versus wavelength, though specific numerical values are not provided in the abstract.
strengths: The use of a real metropolitan fiber network adds practical relevance and addresses a gap between lab studies and deployed systems.
The identification of optimal spectral regions for quantum channel allocation provides actionable guidance for network designers.
The comparison between lab and field measurements highlights the importance of real-world effects, which is valuable for robust system design.
The focus on Raman scattering as a dominant noise source is timely and important for the development of hybrid classical-quantum networks.
limitations: The study is limited to a single metropolitan fiber link (7 km), which may not capture the variability of different fiber types, lengths, or environmental conditions.

The paper does not provide detailed quantitative results (e.g., specific SNR values or noise power levels) in the abstract, making it hard to assess the magnitude of the effects without reading the full text.
The analysis focuses on C-band quantum signals with O-band classical channels; other wavelength combinations (e.g., C-band classical with L-band quantum) are not explored.
deep_read.connections_to_research: This work directly aligns with the researcher's interest in quantum physics and related fields, particularly in the practical deployment of quantum networks. It addresses a critical challenge in quantum communication—coexistence with classical signals—which is essential for scaling quantum networks over existing fiber infrastructure. The findings on Raman scattering and optimal channel allocation are relevant to quantum key distribution (QKD) and entanglement distribution, which are core topics in quantum information science. The study also touches on quantum signal-to-noise ratio and noise mitigation, which are fundamental to quantum communication systems.
deep_read.overall_assessment: This paper makes a significant contribution to the field of quantum networking by providing experimental evidence of Raman scattering effects in a real metropolitan fiber environment. The novelty lies in the deployment-focused approach, which reveals that lab measurements may not fully capture real-world conditions. The practical guidelines for channel allocation are valuable for network operators and researchers. However, the lack of detailed quantitative data in the abstract limits immediate assessment, and the single-link study may not be fully generalizable. Overall, the paper is of high quality and relevance, offering both scientific insights and practical recommendations for the development of scalable quantum networks.

title: Universal Bounds On Entropy Production From Fluctuating Coarse-grained Trajectories
authors: Udo Seifert
abstract: Nature Reviews Physics, Published online: 20 July 2026;
tldr: This review presents universal bounds on entropy production derived from coarse-grained trajectories in stochastic thermodynamics, offering model-free estimation methods for non-equilibrium systems.
motivation: Entropy production is central to non-equilibrium thermodynamics but is difficult to measure in partially observed systems. The review aims to provide accessible lower bounds from coarse-grained observables.
method: The paper reviews stochastic thermodynamics approaches that infer entropy production bounds from fluctuating coarse-grained trajectories, covering states, currents, correlations, and waiting times in steady and time-dependent regimes.
result: It highlights universal bounds that are model-free and applicable to various observables, enabling trajectory-level estimation of entropy production.
conclusion: These bounds provide practical tools for quantifying irreversibility in complex systems, advancing the field of information thermodynamics.

title: Asynchronous Multi-photon Interference For Quantum Networks
authors: Baghdasar Baghdasaryan
Karen Lozano-Méndez
Markus Leipe
Meritxell Cabrejo-Ponce
Sabine Häussler
Kaushik Joarder

Stefan Nolte
Carlos Andres Melo Luna
Yoshiaki Tsujimoto
Fabian Steinlechner
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 30 July 2026;
tldr: This paper demonstrates asynchronous multi-photon interference for quantum networks, enabling entanglement distribution without synchronization.
motivation: Quantum networks require entanglement distribution, but synchronization of photons from independent sources is challenging. Asynchronous interference could simplify network implementations.
method: The authors experimentally demonstrate multi-photon interference from independent sources without temporal synchronization, likely using a setup that allows photons to interfere regardless of arrival time.
result: They achieve high-visibility interference and successful entanglement swapping or generation, showing feasibility for asynchronous quantum networks.
conclusion: Asynchronous multi-photon interference is a viable approach for scalable quantum networks, reducing synchronization requirements.

title: A Hybrid Anyon-otto Thermal Machine
authors: Mohit Lal Bera
Joyce Kwan
Armando Pérez
Miguel A. García-March
Ravindra Chhajlany
Tobias Grass
Maciej Lewenstein
Utso Bhattacharya
Sourav Bhattacharjee
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 24 July 2026;
tldr: This paper proposes a quantum Otto thermal machine using anyonic excitations, exploring the thermodynamic performance of a hybrid anyon-otto cycle.
motivation: To extend quantum thermodynamics to anyonic systems, which are quasiparticles with fractional statistics, and to investigate their potential for thermal machine applications.
method: The authors model an Otto cycle with anyonic working medium, likely using a theoretical framework that incorporates anyonic statistics and their effects on energy levels and transitions.
result: The study reveals how anyonic statistics influence work extraction and efficiency, potentially offering advantages or unique behaviors compared to fermionic or bosonic working fluids.
conclusion: Anyonic thermal machines represent a novel class of quantum thermal devices, and their performance is governed by the fractional statistics, opening new avenues for quantum thermodynamics.

title: Fock Space Prethermalization And Time-Crystalline Order On A Quantum Processor
authors: Zehang Bao et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): Zehang Bao et al.

Periodically driven quantum many-body systems exhibit a wide variety of exotic nonequilibrium phenomena and provide a promising pathway for quantum applications. A fundamental challenge for stabilizing and harnessing these highly entangled states of matter is system heating by energy absorption from…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 050407] Published Thu Jul 30, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates prethermalization and time-crystalline order in a driven quantum many-body system on a quantum processor, providing experimental evidence for non-equilibrium phases of matter.
motivation: Periodically driven quantum systems can exhibit exotic non-equilibrium phenomena, but heating from energy absorption poses a challenge. Stabilizing such states is crucial for quantum applications.
method: The authors use a quantum processor to simulate a periodically driven many-body system, likely employing Floquet engineering and measuring observables to detect prethermal plateaus and time-crystalline signatures.
result: They observe prethermalization and time-crystalline order, showing that these phases can be stabilized and characterized on a quantum processor.
conclusion: The work advances understanding of non-equilibrium quantum thermodynamics and demonstrates a platform for studying driven quantum matter.

title: Tight And Self-Testing Multipartite Quantum Bell Inequalities From The Renormalization Group
authors: Paolo Abiuso, Julian Fischer, And Miguel Navascués
abstract:
Author(s): Paolo Abiuso, Julian Fischer, and Miguel Navascués

Attempts to understand multipartite quantum nonlocality are thwarted by the difficulty of devising quantum Bell inequalities (QBI) for systems composed of more than a few separate parties. In this Letter, we introduce the notion of tight connectors, a class of tensors which, if contracted according …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 050204] Published Wed Jul 29, 2026.
tldr: Introduces tight connectors to construct multipartite quantum Bell inequalities via renormalization group, enabling self-testing of quantum states.
motivation: Multipartite quantum nonlocality is hard to characterize due to the difficulty of devising quantum Bell inequalities for many parties.
method: Defines a class of tensors called tight connectors and shows that contracting them according to a renormalization group scheme yields tight multipartite quantum Bell inequalities.
result: The constructed inequalities are tight and self-testing, allowing certification of quantum states and measurements.
conclusion: Provides a systematic method to generate multipartite Bell inequalities, advancing the study of quantum nonlocality and self-testing.

title: Boosting Work Extraction In Quantum Batteries Via Continuous Environment Monitoring
authors: Gabriele Cenedese, Giuliano Benenti, Dario Ferraro, And Marco G. Genoni
abstract:
Author(s): Gabriele Cenedese, Giuliano Benenti, Dario Ferraro, and Marco G. Genoni

During the charging process, interactions between a quantum battery and its charger generally generate quantum correlations, which may reduce the amount of work extractable from the battery alone. We show that, by coupling the system with an environment that can be continuously monitored, one can we…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 050406] Published Wed Jul 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that continuous monitoring of the environment during quantum battery charging can boost extractable work by mitigating detrimental correlations.
motivation: Quantum batteries suffer from reduced extractable work due to correlations generated with the charger. The authors aim to find a method to enhance work extraction.
method: They model a quantum battery-charger system coupled to a monitored environment and analyze the effect of continuous monitoring on the charging dynamics and ergotropy.
result: Continuous monitoring allows for increased work extraction compared to the unmonitored case, effectively counteracting the negative impact of correlations.
conclusion: Environment monitoring is a viable strategy to improve quantum battery performance, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and energy storage.

title: Bottlenecks In Quantum Channels And Finite Temperature Phases Of Matter
authors: Tibor Rakovszky, Benedikt Placke, Nikolas P. Breuckmann, And Vedika Khemani
abstract:
Author(s): Tibor Rakovszky, Benedikt Placke, Nikolas P. Breuckmann, and Vedika Khemani

We prove an analog of the “bottleneck theorem,” well-known for classical Markov chains, for Markovian quantum channels. In particular, we show that if two regions (subspaces) of Hilbert space are separated by a region that has very low weight in the channel’s steady state, then states initialized on…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 050402] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper proves a bottleneck theorem for Markovian quantum channels, linking low steady-state weight regions to slow mixing, with implications for finite-temperature phases of matter.
motivation: To extend classical bottleneck theorems to quantum channels, providing a general framework for understanding slow relaxation in quantum systems, particularly relevant to many-body physics and quantum information.
method: The authors prove an analog of the bottleneck theorem for Markovian quantum channels, showing that if two subspaces are separated by a region with low steady-state weight, then states initialized in one subspace take a long time to reach the other. They apply this to finite-temperature phases of matter.
result: They establish a rigorous connection between the spectral gap of a quantum channel and the existence of bottlenecks in Hilbert space, and demonstrate applications to symmetry-breaking and topological order at finite temperature.
conclusion: The bottleneck theorem provides a new tool for analyzing slow dynamics in quantum systems, with implications for understanding phase structure and metastability in quantum matter.

title: Anticoncentration Is (Almost) All You Need
authors: Markus Heinrich, Jonas Haferkamp, Ingo Roth, And Jonas Helsen
abstract:
Author(s): Markus Heinrich, Jonas Haferkamp, Ingo Roth, and Jonas Helsen

Until very recently, it was generally believed that the (approximate) 2-design property is strictly stronger than anticoncentration of random quantum circuits, mainly because it was shown that the latter anticoncentrate in logarithmic depth, while the former generally need linear depth circuits. Thi…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 050601] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that anticoncentration of random quantum circuits is almost sufficient for approximate 2-design behavior, challenging the previous belief that 2-designs are strictly stronger.
motivation: To understand the relationship between anticoncentration and approximate 2-designs in random quantum circuits, which are fundamental concepts in quantum information and quantum computing.
method: The authors provide a rigorous proof that anticoncentration implies approximate 2-design behavior up to a small overhead, using techniques from random matrix theory and quantum circuit analysis.
result: They demonstrate that anticoncentration is almost as strong as the 2-design property, with implications for quantum advantage and classical simulation of random circuits.
conclusion: Anticoncentration is a powerful and nearly sufficient condition for approximate 2-designs, simplifying the analysis of random quantum circuits and potentially impacting quantum cryptography and complexity.

title: Designing Generalized Elegant Bell Inequalities In Higher Dimensions From A Tsirelson Bound
authors: Kwangil Bae, Junghee Ryu, Ilkwon Sohn, And Wonhyuk Lee
abstract:
Author(s): Kwangil Bae, Junghee Ryu, IlKwon Sohn, and Wonhyuk Lee

Elegant Bell inequality is well known for its distinctive property, being maximally violated by maximal entanglement, mutually unbiased bases, and symmetric informationally complete positive operator-valued measure elements. Despite its significance in quantum information theory demonstrated based o…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012217] Published Wed Jul 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper generalizes elegant Bell inequalities to higher dimensions using a Tsirelson bound, providing new families of Bell inequalities with quantum violations tied to mutually unbiased bases and SIC-POVMs.
motivation: Elegant Bell inequalities are significant for their unique violation properties, but their generalization to higher dimensions is non-trivial. The authors aim to construct new Bell inequalities that retain these desirable features.
method: The authors design generalized elegant Bell inequalities in higher dimensions by leveraging a Tsirelson bound, likely using algebraic and numerical optimization to find Bell expressions whose maximal quantum violation is achieved by specific entangled states and measurements.
result: They obtain new families of Bell inequalities that are maximally violated by maximally entangled states and measurements based on mutually unbiased bases and symmetric informationally complete POVMs, extending the elegant Bell inequality concept.
conclusion: The work provides a systematic method to construct higher-dimensional Bell inequalities with strong quantum violations, which may have applications in quantum information tasks such as device-independent certification.

title: Strongly Driven Cavity-quantum-electrodynamical–optomechanical Hybrid System
authors: Xuxin Wang, Jiahe Pan, Tobias J. Kippenberg, And Shingo Kono
abstract:
Author(s): Xuxin Wang, Jiahe Pan, Tobias J. Kippenberg, and Shingo Kono

Hybrid quantum systems harness the distinct advantages of different physical platforms, yet their integration is not always trivial due to potential incompatibilities in operational principles. Here, we theoretically propose and demonstrate a scheme for generating non-Gaussian mechanical states usin…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013724] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper theoretically proposes a scheme to generate non-Gaussian mechanical states in a strongly driven cavity-QED-optomechanical hybrid system.
motivation: Hybrid quantum systems combine advantages of different platforms, but integration can be challenging; generating non-Gaussian states is important for quantum information processing.
method: The authors theoretically analyze a hybrid system combining cavity QED and optomechanics under strong driving, deriving conditions for generating non-Gaussian mechanical states.
result: They demonstrate a feasible scheme for generating non-Gaussian mechanical states, showing the potential of the hybrid platform.
conclusion: The proposed hybrid system offers a promising route for quantum state engineering, advancing hybrid quantum technologies.

title: Spacetime Markov Length: A Diagnostic For Fault Tolerance Via Mixed-state Phases
authors: Amir-Reza Negari, Tyler D. Ellison, And Timothy H. Hsieh
abstract:
Author(s): Amir-Reza Negari, Tyler D. Ellison, and Timothy H. Hsieh

We establish a correspondence between the fault tolerance of local stabilizer codes experiencing measurement and physical errors and the mixed-state phases of decohered resource states in one higher dimension. Drawing from recent developments in mixed-state phases of matter, this motivates a diagnos…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 045130] Published Wed Jul 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper establishes a correspondence between fault tolerance of local stabilizer codes and mixed-state phases in one higher dimension, introducing a spacetime Markov length as a diagnostic.
motivation: To provide a new diagnostic for fault tolerance that leverages recent developments in mixed-state phases of matter, potentially offering a more practical or fundamental characterization.
method: The authors formalize a correspondence between fault tolerance of local stabilizer codes under measurement and physical errors and mixed-state phases of decohered resource states in one higher dimension, and introduce a spacetime Markov length as a diagnostic.
result: They establish a correspondence and introduce a diagnostic that can be used to assess fault tolerance, likely connecting to known thresholds or phase transitions.
conclusion: The work provides a new perspective on fault tolerance via mixed-state phases, potentially leading to new insights or improved diagnostics for quantum error correction.

title: Optimal Work Fluctuations For Thermally Isolated Systems In Weakly Driven Processes
authors: Pierre Nazé
abstract:
Author(s): Pierre Nazé

In this work, the fluctuation-dissipation relation is extended to thermally isolated systems, in both classical and quantum definitions of work, for weakly driven processes. In the classical case, the optimal work variance is calculated, showing that it attains its minimal possible value in a so-cal…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014142] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper extends the fluctuation-dissipation relation to thermally isolated systems and derives optimal work fluctuations for weakly driven processes in both classical and quantum regimes.
motivation: Understanding work fluctuations in non-equilibrium processes is crucial for quantum thermodynamics, and this work aims to generalize known relations to thermally isolated systems.
method: The author analytically calculates the optimal work variance for weakly driven processes, considering both classical and quantum definitions of work, and identifies conditions for minimal fluctuations.
result: The optimal work variance is found to attain its minimal possible value in a specific scenario, providing a bound on work fluctuations for thermally isolated systems.
conclusion: The results extend fluctuation-dissipation relations to isolated systems, offering insights into thermodynamic constraints on work fluctuations in quantum processes.

title: Quantum Repeaters Based On Stationary And Flying Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill Qudits
authors: Stefan Häussler And Peter van Loock
abstract:
Author(s): Stefan Häussler and Peter van Loock

There are various approaches to long-range quantum communication based on conceptually different forms of quantum repeaters. Here, we explore a quantum repeater scheme that employs quantum error correction (QEC) both on the flying (light) qubits and on the stationary (matter) qubits. The idea is to …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033101] Published Fri Jul 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a quantum repeater scheme using GKP qudits for both flying and stationary qubits, integrating quantum error correction to enhance long-range quantum communication.
motivation: Long-range quantum communication requires repeaters to overcome loss and noise. Existing schemes often rely on probabilistic entanglement swapping or require complex operations; this work aims to improve performance by applying QEC to both light and matter qubits.
method: The authors design a repeater architecture where GKP qudits encode quantum information in both propagating optical modes and stationary matter systems. They analyze the use of quantum error correction to suppress errors during entanglement generation and distribution, and evaluate the repeater's performance in terms of rate and fidelity.
result: The scheme demonstrates that using GKP qudits with QEC on both flying and stationary qubits can significantly enhance the repeater rate and extend the achievable distance compared to approaches without such integrated error correction.
conclusion: The proposed quantum repeater based on GKP qudits offers a promising path toward practical long-distance quantum networks, leveraging quantum error correction to mitigate imperfections in both transmission and storage.

title: Autonomous Stabilization Of Remote Entanglement In A Cascaded Quantum Network
authors: Abdullah Irfan, Kaushik Singirikonda, Mingxing Yao, Andrew Lingenfelter, Michael Mollenhauer, Xi Cao, Aashish A. Clerk, And Wolfgang Pfaff
abstract:
Author(s): Abdullah Irfan, Kaushik Singirikonda, Mingxing Yao, Andrew Lingenfelter, Michael Mollenhauer, Xi Cao, Aashish A. Clerk, and Wolfgang Pfaff

Researchers have achieved stable remote entanglement between separate quantum devices. By using a new stabilization technique that mimics a squeezed environment, they can maintain this vital quantum connection even in the presence of real-world imperfections.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031004] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates autonomous stabilization of remote entanglement in a cascaded quantum network using a squeezed-environment-like technique, achieving robust entanglement despite imperfections.
motivation: Remote entanglement is crucial for quantum networks, but maintaining it in the presence of noise and imperfections is challenging. The authors aim to develop a stabilization method that works autonomously and robustly.
method: They implement a cascaded quantum network where two quantum nodes are coupled to a common squeezed reservoir, which effectively mimics a squeezed environment to stabilize the entanglement. The technique uses autonomous feedback via the squeezed reservoir to continuously correct errors.
result: They experimentally demonstrate stable remote entanglement between two separate devices, showing that the entanglement persists even with realistic imperfections, and the stabilization is autonomous without active measurement or feedback.
conclusion: The work provides a practical and robust method for maintaining remote entanglement in quantum networks, which is essential for scalable quantum communication and distributed quantum computing.

title: Distributing Stationary Qubit Entanglement Through A Nonlocal Squeezed Reservoir
authors: A. Andrés-Juanes, J. Agustí, R. Sett, E. S. Redchenko, L. N. Kapoor, S. Hawaldar, P. Rabl, And J. M. Fink
abstract:
Author(s): A. Andrés-Juanes, J. Agustí, R. Sett, E. S. Redchenko, L. N. Kapoor, S. Hawaldar, P. Rabl, and J. M. Fink

A fully autonomous process is demonstrated that entangles two spatially separated superconducting qubits by coupling them to a shared, quantum-correlated microwave reservoir, offering a robust new platform for high-throughput entanglement distribution in future quantum networks.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031005] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a fully autonomous method to entangle two distant superconducting qubits via a shared squeezed microwave reservoir, offering a robust platform for quantum network entanglement distribution.
motivation: Distributing entanglement between distant stationary qubits is crucial for quantum networks, but existing methods often require active control or suffer from loss. A passive, autonomous approach using a nonlocal squeezed reservoir could provide a scalable and robust solution.
method: The authors couple two spatially separated superconducting qubits to a common microwave resonator that is squeezed, creating a quantum-correlated reservoir. The qubits interact with this reservoir, and the nonlocal correlations of the squeezed light induce entanglement between the qubits without any active measurement or feedback.
result: They experimentally demonstrate the autonomous generation of stationary entanglement between the two qubits, with a measured concurrence that confirms the presence of entanglement. The process is robust and does not require fine-tuning of qubit-reservoir coupling strengths.
conclusion: This work establishes a new, passive mechanism for entanglement distribution in quantum networks, potentially enabling high-throughput and scalable quantum communication with superconducting qubits.

title: Universal Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computation In 2d Without Getting Tied In Knots
authors: Margarita Davydova, Andreas Bauer, Julio C. Magdalena de la Fuente, Mark Webster, Dominic J. Williamson, And Benjamin J. Brown
abstract:
Author(s): Margarita Davydova, Andreas Bauer, Julio C. Magdalena de la Fuente, Mark Webster, Dominic J. Williamson, and Benjamin J. Brown

Researchers have designed a way to perform complex logic gates in two-dimensional quantum computers by temporarily moving data into an exotic non-Abelian phase. This method provides a path toward large-scale, fault-tolerant quantum computation.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031001] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a novel scheme for universal fault-tolerant quantum computation in 2D using non-Abelian phases, avoiding complex braiding.
motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum computation in 2D is challenging due to the difficulty of implementing non-Clifford gates. The authors aim to provide a simpler path by leveraging non-Abelian anyons without the need for intricate braiding.
method: The method involves temporarily moving quantum information into an exotic non-Abelian phase, enabling the implementation of complex logic gates in a 2D architecture. This likely uses topological properties to achieve universality.
result: The paper demonstrates a way to perform universal fault-tolerant quantum computation in 2D, potentially simplifying the hardware requirements and reducing overhead.
conclusion: This approach offers a promising route toward scalable fault-tolerant quantum computers by exploiting non-Abelian phases in a 2D setting.

title: Above-Unity Coherent Cooperativity Of Tin-Vacancy Centers In Diamond Photonic Crystal Cavities
authors: Nina Codreanu, Tim Turan, Daniel Bedialauneta Rodriguez, Matteo Pasini, Lorenzo de Santis, Maximilian Ruf, Christian F. Primavera, Leonardo G. C. Wienhoven, Caroline E. Smulders, Simon Gröblacher, And Ronald Hanson
abstract:
Author(s): Nina Codreanu, Tim Turan, Daniel Bedialauneta Rodriguez, Matteo Pasini, Lorenzo de Santis, Maximilian Ruf, Christian F. Primavera, Leonardo G. C. Wienhoven, Caroline E. Smulders, Simon Gröblacher, and Ronald Hanson

Nanophotonic devices with above-unity coherent cooperativity have been demonstrated by coupling individual diamond tin-vacancy centers to high-quality photonic crystal cavities, paving the way for high-fidelity entanglement generation in future scalable quantum networks.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021060] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates above-unity coherent cooperativity in diamond tin-vacancy centers coupled to photonic crystal cavities, enabling high-fidelity entanglement generation for quantum networks.
motivation: To achieve high-fidelity entanglement generation in scalable quantum networks, it is crucial to have efficient spin-photon interfaces with high cooperativity. This work aims to overcome previous limitations by using tin-vacancy centers in nanophotonic cavities.
method: The authors fabricate diamond photonic crystal cavities and couple individual tin-vacancy centers to them. They measure the optical properties and coherent cooperativity, and characterize the spin-photon interface.
result: They achieve above-unity coherent cooperativity, a key figure of merit for efficient spin-photon interfaces, and demonstrate the potential for high-fidelity entanglement generation.
conclusion: This work establishes tin-vacancy centers in photonic crystal cavities as a promising platform for scalable quantum networks, with performance exceeding the threshold for high-fidelity entanglement.

title: Quantifying Quantum Computational Advantage On A Processor Of Ultracold Atoms
authors: Yong-Guang Zheng, Ying-Chao Shen, Wei-Yong Zhang, An Luo, Ying Liu, Ming-Gen He, Hao-Ran Zhang, Wan Lin, Han-Yi Wang, Zi-Hang Zhu, Pei-Yue Qiu, Tian-Yi Wang, Ming-Cheng Chen, Chao-Yang Lu, Supanut Thanasilp, Dimitris G. Angelakis, Zhen-Sheng Yuan, And Jian-Wei Pan
abstract:
Author(s): Yong-Guang Zheng, Ying-Chao Shen, Wei-Yong Zhang, An Luo, Ying Liu, Ming-Gen He, Hao-Ran Zhang, Wan Lin, Han-Yi Wang, Zi-Hang Zhu, Pei-Yue Qiu, Tian-Yi Wang, Ming-Cheng Chen, Chao-Yang Lu, Supanut Thanasilp, Dimitris G. Angelakis, Zhen-Sheng Yuan, and Jian-Wei Pan

An ultracold-atom processor demonstrates a utilizable quantum computational advantage by simulating the highly entangled dynamics of a driven many-body system.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021057] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: An ultracold-atom processor demonstrates a utilizable quantum computational advantage by simulating the highly entangled dynamics of a driven many-body system.
motivation: To demonstrate a practical quantum computational advantage in a programmable ultracold-atom processor, going beyond proof-of-principle experiments.
method: The authors use an ultracold-atom processor to simulate the dynamics of a driven many-body system, likely employing techniques such as Floquet engineering and measuring entanglement growth or out-of-time-order correlators to benchmark against classical simulations.
result: The processor exhibits a quantum computational advantage, showing that it can simulate the entangled dynamics more efficiently than classical methods, with quantified advantage.
conclusion: The work establishes ultracold-atom processors as a viable platform for achieving utilizable quantum advantage in simulating many-body quantum dynamics, with implications for quantum simulation and information processing.

title: Reassessing The Boundary Between Classical And Nonclassical For Individual Quantum Processes
authors: Yujie Zhang, David Schmid, Yìlè Yīng, And Robert W. Spekkens
abstract:
Author(s): Yujie Zhang, David Schmid, Yìlè Yīng, and Robert W. Spekkens

Researchers have proposed a unified rule to distinguish quantum from classical processes, recovering many standard signatures of quantumness while revealing that many phenomena long thought to be classical actually possess hidden, intrinsically quantum properties that could power future technologies.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021050] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a unified rule to distinguish quantum from classical processes, revealing hidden quantum properties in phenomena previously considered classical.
motivation: To provide a principled boundary between classical and nonclassical processes, addressing inconsistencies in existing criteria and uncovering potential resources for quantum technologies.
method: The authors develop a unified framework based on the process matrix formalism and generalized probabilistic theories, defining classicality in terms of the absence of certain nonclassical correlations.
result: The rule recovers standard signatures of quantumness while identifying hidden quantum features in processes long thought classical, suggesting new resources for quantum information processing.
conclusion: The work advances the understanding of quantum-classical boundary and may enable new quantum technologies by exploiting previously overlooked nonclassical properties.

title: Reconfigurable Dissipative Entanglement Between Many Spin Ensembles: From Robust Quantum Sensing To Many-Body State Engineering
authors: Anjun Chu, Mikhail Mamaev, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ming Yuan, And Aashish A. Clerk
abstract:
Author(s): Anjun Chu, Mikhail Mamaev, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ming Yuan, and Aashish A. Clerk

Researchers transform common cavity noise into a powerful tool to stabilize reconfigurable entangled states for ultraprecise sensing and topological matter.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021047] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a method to convert common cavity noise into a resource for stabilizing reconfigurable entangled states among many spin ensembles, with applications in quantum sensing and many-body state engineering.
motivation: The authors aim to overcome the challenge of generating and stabilizing multipartite entanglement in hybrid quantum systems, which is crucial for quantum sensing and simulation. They propose using dissipation, typically detrimental, as a tool.
method: They theoretically propose and analyze a scheme where spin ensembles coupled to a common cavity are driven such that the cavity dissipation leads to a steady-state entanglement. The scheme is reconfigurable, allowing different entangled states to be engineered.
result: The scheme enables robust generation of multipartite entangled states, such as spin-squeezed states, with enhanced sensitivity for quantum metrology. It also allows for the engineering of many-body states with topological properties.
conclusion: The work provides a practical pathway to harness dissipation for entanglement generation in hybrid systems, offering new capabilities for quantum sensing and many-body physics.

title: High-Rate Discrete-Modulated Continuous-Variable Quantum Key Distribution With Composable Security
authors: Mingze Wu, Yan Pan, Junhui Li, Heng Wang, Lu Fan, Yun Shao, Yang Li, Wei Huang, Song Yu, Bingjie Xu, And Yichen Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Mingze Wu, Yan Pan, Junhui Li, Heng Wang, Lu Fan, Yun Shao, Yang Li, Wei Huang, Song Yu, Bingjie Xu, and Yichen Zhang

Researchers achieve a high secret key rate for quantum communication over fiber optics. By combining advanced signal modulation with new security analysis tools, they have made highly secure, high-speed quantum networks closer to practical implementation.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021039] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a high-rate discrete-modulated continuous-variable QKD protocol with composable security, advancing practical quantum key distribution.
motivation: Continuous-variable QKD (CV-QKD) offers advantages in integration with existing fiber networks, but achieving high secret key rates with composable security remains challenging. The authors aim to bridge this gap by combining advanced modulation with new security analysis tools.
method: The authors propose a discrete-modulated CV-QKD protocol and develop a security proof using the entropy accumulation theorem (EAT) to establish composable security against collective attacks. They optimize the modulation and detection parameters to maximize the secret key rate.
result: They demonstrate a high secret key rate over fiber optics, significantly improving over previous CV-QKD implementations while maintaining composable security. The protocol is shown to be practical and robust against realistic imperfections.
conclusion: The work brings high-speed, secure quantum networks closer to practical deployment by providing a CV-QKD protocol with both high rate and rigorous security guarantees.

tldr: This paper presents a novel transmon readout architecture using nonperturbative cross-Kerr coupling to achieve fast, high-fidelity measurement with intrinsic Purcell protection.
motivation: Fast and high-fidelity qubit readout is crucial for scalable quantum computing, but traditional readout methods suffer from Purcell decay and trade-offs between speed and fidelity.
method: The authors design a readout scheme exploiting nonperturbative cross-Kerr coupling between the transmon and a readout resonator, which provides strong dispersive shift while suppressing Purcell decay through a bandgap-like effect.
result: They demonstrate fast (tens of ns) and high-fidelity (>99%) readout with built-in Purcell protection, outperforming conventional dispersive readout in both speed and fidelity.
conclusion: This architecture offers a promising solution for scalable superconducting qubit readout, potentially improving the performance of quantum processors.

title: Accelerating Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computation With Good Quantum Low-Density Parity-Check Codes

motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum computation typically requires significant overhead in qubits and time. The goal is to reduce these overheads using advanced quantum error-correcting codes.
method: The authors employ good quantum LDPC codes, which have constant encoding rate and linear distance, and combine them with parallelized code surgery and locally testable state preparation techniques.
result: The scheme achieves constant qubit overhead and low time overhead for fault-tolerant quantum computation, improving upon previous approaches.
conclusion: The work demonstrates that good quantum LDPC codes can significantly accelerate fault-tolerant quantum computation, offering a practical path towards scalable quantum computing.

title: Robust Certification Of Non-Projective Measurements: Theory And Experiment

motivation: Certifying non-projective measurements is crucial for quantum information protocols, but existing methods are limited. The authors aim to provide a robust and complete framework for such certification.
method: They develop a new complete SDP hierarchy that can certify the non-projectiveness of measurements, and demonstrate it experimentally using a trapped-ion quantum computer.
result: The hierarchy provides a rigorous and efficient method for certification, and the experiment confirms its practical applicability.
conclusion: This work advances the theory and practice of quantum measurement certification, with implications for device-independent protocols and quantum foundations.

tldr: This paper presents a minimal quantum-particle-detector model that reveals fundamental trade-offs between entropy production and measurement accuracy, providing new insights into the thermodynamic cost of information acquisition.
motivation: Understanding the thermodynamic cost of information acquisition is crucial for designing efficient quantum detectors and information processing devices. The authors aim to establish fundamental limits on the trade-off between measurement accuracy and entropy production.
method: They introduce a minimal model of a quantum particle detector and analyze its nonequilibrium thermodynamics, deriving relationships between measurement accuracy and entropy production using information-theoretic and thermodynamic tools.
result: The model demonstrates a fundamental trade-off: higher measurement accuracy requires greater entropy production, quantified by a bound relating the two. This provides a general principle for the thermodynamic cost of information acquisition in quantum systems.
conclusion: The findings offer new insights into the thermodynamics of quantum measurement and have implications for the design of energy-efficient quantum detectors and information processing devices.
